items.actClause: AN ACT to authorize the board of trustees of the state university of New York to establish an advanced weather observing network across the state
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S5315

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to authorize the board of trustees of the state
university of New York to establish an advanced weather observing
network across the state

PURPOSE:

Authorizes the board of trustees of the state university to contract
with the research foundation of the state university for the establish-
ment of a statewide network of 125 surface weather stations.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: States the legislative findings that the establishment by the
state university of New York of an advanced weather observing network to
expand weather detection coverage across the state serves the public
interest.

Section 2: Authorizes the SUNY Board of Trustees or its designee(s) to
contract to make lands available to the Research Foundation for the
State University of New York for the purpose of constructing, install-
ing, erecting, maintaining, replacing, testing, calibrating and decon-
structing surface weather stations with the approval of the president of
the campus upon which the land is located. Rights of ingress and egress
access to the plot of land would also be authorized for such purpose.
Grounds would be limited to plots of contiguous land not to exceed 400
linear feet per site (less than .23 acres) and each site is required to
be located at least 300 feet from the nearest obstacle or potential heat
source. Contracts for such properties would be limited to 40 years. In
the event that the land ceases to be used for the purpose describe here-
in, the contract would terminate immediately and the land would be
required to be restored to its original state.

Section 3: Requires any contacts entered into as a result of this act
must include prevailing wage.

Section 4: States that nothing in this bill shall waive, impair any
right or benefit of employees of SUNY and any work performed on property
that ordinarily would be performed by employees will continue to be
performed by employees.

Section 5: All contracts executed pursuant to this legislation shall
include indemnity provision.

Section 6: Requires contracts entered due to this act between the
research foundation for the state university of New York and parties
contracting with the research foundation shall be awarded by competitive
bidding process.

Section 7: Establishes a three year time frame within which any such
contracts shall be executed.

Section 8: Insofar as the provisions of this act are inconsistent with
the provisions of any other provision of law, the provisions of this act
shall be controlling.

Section 9: This act shall take effect immediately.

JUSTIFICATION:

Studies have shown that during recent decades there has been a clear
trend toward more extreme precipitation in the northeastern United
States, including New York State. Since 2006, there have been 20 FEMA
declared disasters and emergencies in New York State. Four of these
events were associated with winter weather (snowstorms and/or lake-ef-
fect snow) while the other sixteen were associated with severe weather
and/or flooding (including tropical systems Irene and Sandy).  According
to a 2011 study published by the American Meteorological Society, New
York is also the most vulnerable of the 50 states to the negative
economic effects of weather variability.

There is a need and opportunity to strengthen the New York State infras-
tructure and economy with an enhanced Weather Enterprise based on model-
ing and prediction research combined with enhanced observing systems.
Federal funding ($23.6 million) from FEMA through the NYS Division of
Homeland Security and Emergency Services has been secured by the
Research Foundation for the State University of New York on behalf of
University at Albany scientists for a weather station network consisting
of up to 125 surface weather stations, with at least one in every coun-
ty. The State University system's geographic diversity, particularly in
Upstate NY make SUNY campuses suitable potential sites for these weather
stations. However, the Research Foundation for the State University of
New York ("RF") is not currently authorized to undertake the activities
necessary to construct or maintain these towers on SUNY campuses. Leases
or transfers of ownership for these plots of land are not necessary;
however, a contract such as a use permit authorizing the RF to
construct, install, erect, maintain, replace, test, calibrate, and
deconstruct the weather station along with access rights to the plot of
land for such activities would be sufficient. Under this b ill, lands on
SUNY campuses would not be available for such contracts unless the Pres-
ident of the campus authorizes the use of the land for such purposes.

The National Weather Service is currently served by 27 high quality
weather stations which, while valuable, leave significant gaps in the
network. New York would benefit from more accurate high quality atmo-
spheric data, transmitted every five minutes by the new weather
stations. Real-time data such as rainfall totals, temperature change,
and wind monitoring help emergency management officials assess situ-
ations and direct resources efficiently, whether to evacuate residents
or mitigate damages for vulnerable sectors such as road and rail trans-
portation, aviation, energy, agriculture, tourism, and commerce. As an
example, the additional data will lead to more accurate short-term model
predictions to help the State Transportation Department decide when and
where to deploy crews during blizzards and other extreme weather events.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

This is a new bill.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

The project has been awarded $23.6 million in Federal funding.

EFFECTIVE DATE:

This act shall take effect immediately.
